summary: Cherokee County tower listed as gone. The 1933 Texas Forest Service survey station (NGS datasheet BY2737) is linked in a 2011 Texas tower list to the Loc 1 coordinates; a separate Maydelle entry sits at the Loc 2 coordinates.

facts.design: Standard-type steel lookout tower, painted gray
facts.status_note: FFLA index marks Maydelle (Loc 1) as Gone. No removal date or cause is given. The 2011 Texas tower list ties datasheet BY2737, the 1933 survey station, to the Loc 1 coordinates.

events.note: Survey station description (NGS datasheet BY2737) gives 1933 as the build year and places the station four miles west of Maydelle. The 2011 Texas tower list links datasheet BY2737 to the Loc 1 coordinates.
June 2, 1939 Rusk Cherokeean item names the tower Tower No. 8 in Maydelle State Forest, four miles southwest of Maydelle.

February 14, 1946 Rusk Cherokeean item: Forest Patrolman Ray Sides at the Maydelle lookout tower reported and suppressed one of nine Cherokee County fires in January 1946. The item says that fire was caused by an incendiarist.
Forest patrolman at the Maydelle lookout tower: Ray Sides in the February 14 and May 9, 1946 items, Roy Sides in the April 11, 1946 item.
Alto Herald, January 17, 1952: J.A. Benge, who had managed the Alto tower, was moving to Maydelle to take over the fire tower there.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The survey description says four miles west of Maydelle; the June 1939 item says four miles southwest. Both agree on about four miles. The story gives both and does not choose.
The February 14 and May 9, 1946 items say Ray Sides; the April 11, 1946 item says Roy Sides. The story gives the spelling in each item.

resolved_conflicts.field: which Maydelle site the 1933 tower occupies
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 2011 tower list has two Maydelle entries. The one at 31.78400, -95.36503 sits at the Loc 1 coordinates and cites datasheet BY2737, the station the Forest Lookouts page describes as built in 1933. The one at 31.81958, -95.30931 sits at the Loc 2 coordinates and lists TFS as its source, with no datasheet. The story reads the two pages together as pointing the 1933 tower to Loc 1, hedged. The earlier reading that it might be Loc 2 rested on the Loc 2 entry alone and is superseded.

notes_for_editor: The history rests on one page (Forest Lookouts Maydelle), which quotes the NGS station description for datasheet BY2737 and 1939-1952 Rusk Cherokeean and Alto Herald items. Fact-check on 2026-10-21 found the 2011 Texas tower list entry at 31.78400, -95.36503, which cites datasheet BY2737 and sits at the Loc 1 coordinates; the earlier draft missed it and said no source ties the 1933 tower to Loc 1. The story now reads the two pages together as pointing the 1933 tower to Loc 1, and no longer suggests Loc 2. The Loc 2 entry at 31.81958, -95.30931 is still reported separately. Using the town coordinates in the Wikipedia Maydelle article (31.80083, -95.30250), Loc 1 is about 3.8 miles west-southwest of town and Loc 2 about 1.4 miles north-northwest, which also fits the survey's 'four miles W' better for Loc 1; that is the researcher's arithmetic, not a sourced claim. The sibling record us-tx-maydelle-loc-2 (story says 'The Maydelle tower stands') attributes the same survey to the standing Loc 2 tower. That conflicts with this record and must be reconciled before publishing. Height converted from 110 ft to 33.5 m. No source gives access, a visit route or the site today. Two WebSearch calls and about six page reads used.
